events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
This case cannot be adjudicated on the merits because the fact table records a threat in the booking chat. At 09:54 the driver wrote "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." [F12], and the threat keyword table flagged "find you" in that same message [F13]. That is intimidation language falling squarely within SAFE-1, which is a mandatory escalation trigger (identical to the trace's ✓ SAFE-1 element), so the correct disposition is escalate with a factual summary rather than any ruling on the fee [F12][F13][SAFE-1]. The rider's complaint expressly relies on this message and both advocates concede the content and the flag (driver advocate's C4 concession) [F12][F13][SAFE-1].

Timeline for the reviewer: the ride was accepted at 09:47:00 and cancelled by the driver at 09:54:25, 7 min 25 s later, with a $6.61 cancellation fee on record [F4][F8]. The driver statement says he cancelled as a no-show after waiting over four minutes [F14]. GPS shows his closest approach 38 m from pickup [F1], first entry into the 200 m radius at 09:50:05 with 4 min 20 s cumulative time inside it [F2], and a 4 min 0 s stationary period at 39 m from pickup running to the moment of cancellation [F3]; the platform recorded arrival at 09:50:05 [F5]. Because the cancellation was by the driver on a no-show claim [F14], the $6.61 must be tested under NS-1 (all three elements) and, on any failure, NS-2 full refund [F4][F14][NS-0][NS-1][NS-2]. That analysis is where the disputed point lies.

The material dispute for the human reviewer is an unresolved system-record conflict on NS-1(i): F6 states the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45, 42 m from pickup, with 3 min 40 s inside the radius afterwards, while F7 states driver_pressed_here_at is null [F6][F7]. Both advocates now agree the tap condition is contested (rider C2 narrowing; driver's own weaknesses admitted) [F6][F7][NS-1]. Under NS-1(ii) and (iii) the location and duration limbs look met on the GPS records [F1][F2][F3][F5][NS-1], but the "I'm Here" limb is not yet settled, and NS-2 would refund the $6.61 in full if any limb fails [F8][F6][F7][NS-1][NS-2]; if the tap is credited, NS-2's add-on flag would not apply because GPS does place the driver inside the radius [F6][F3][NS-2]. claims.assertion: The driver cancelled the trip, and his own written statement admits he cancelled claiming the rider was a no-show (F14), so the validity of the $6.61 cancellation fee is governed by NS-1/NS-2, not by the passenger-cancellation rule.

Although GPS shows the driver was within 200 m of the pickup from 09:50:05 and stayed there 4 min 20 s (F2, F3), the timeline contains an internal conflict over the 'I'm Here' tap: F6 says the tap occurred at 09:50:45 while F7 says the driver never tapped 'I'm Here'. Because the driver never tapped, at most one of the two records is correct and NS-1(i) is not clearly satisfied.

The driver tapped 'I'm Here' (if at all) at 09:50:45 while 42 m from the pickup point, and the platform recorded arrival there; rider's own messages show he was actively responding ('2 min, coming', F11), so the rider was engaged and contactable, not a no-show in the ordinary sense.

The driver's chat #3 at 09:54 — 'Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it' — triggered the threat keyword filter (F12, F13). This is threatening and intimidating language directed at the rider in the course of the booking.
Because a threat/intimidation message appears in the chat record, the case cannot be decided by automated fee adjudication and must be escalated to human review with a fact summary.
The fee at stake is exactly $6.61, recorded on the fare record with no surge applied (F8, F9), which is the full cancellation-fee amount that NS-2 makes refundable when NS-1 is not satisfied.

The driver's own statement confirms the fee was triggered by the no-show claim rather than by any rider cancellation, and his account shows no prior disputes (F14, F19), so the cancellation consequence for this trip rests entirely on the NS-1 criteria examined above.

The rider's own chat message '2 min, coming' at 09:52 (F11) followed by cancellation at 09:54:25 (F4) supports the driver's narrative (F14) that the rider did not board within a reasonable time.
The rider's profile shows 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F18), which the other side may use to suggest a pattern of late boarding rather than one-off delay.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled with a valid no-show reason: he was at the pickup point when he cancelled, his closest approach being 38 m at 09:53:15 and he was 39 m from the pickup while stationary 09:50:25–09:54:25.

The driver waited far beyond the 3-minute threshold: he first entered the 200 m pickup radius at 09:50:05 and had 4 min 20 s cumulative time within that radius before cancelling, having cancelled 4 min 20 s after the platform recorded his arrival.

The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:50:45, 42 m from the pickup point (i.e. inside the 200 m pickup radius), and remained within 200 m for 3 min 40 s after the tap, so the 'I'm Here' + >3 minutes waiting requirements are met.
The $6.61 cancellation fee was properly imposed and correctly recorded, with no surge component inflating it, so the fee is supported and needs no adjustment on the merits.

No traffic incident or speed-band record exists on the route in the trip window and the weather was fair, so there is no factual basis for treating this as anything other than an ordinary no-show cancellation by the driver.

The rider has 3 disputes in 90 d with 2 upheld no-show disputes, whereas the driver has 1176 trips in 90 d with 0 disputes and 0 upheld, so the rider's credibility and pattern of repeat no-show claims should be weighed (profile used only as supporting context, not to decide the fee).

weaknesses: Chat #3 at 09:54 from the driver reads 'Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it.' [threat], with threat keywords detected ('find you') in the same message (F12, F13) — this is a SAFE-1 trigger and the rider's complaint expressly relies on it; it may drive the case to escalate rather than a merits ruling on the fee, and it badly damages the driver's conduct record.

The timeline is internally inconsistent: F6 records the driver tapping 'I'm Here' at 09:50:45, 42 m from pick-up, while F7 states driver_pressed_here_at is null. The rider will press F7 as a NS-1(i) failure, and the system-record conflict cannot be resolved in the driver's favour without choosing F6 over F7.

The rider's message '2 min, coming' at 09:52 (F11) is a statement, and the driver's written claim of waiting over 4 minutes (F14) is only consistent with, not proven by, the GPS records (F2, F3, F5); the fee outcome rests on the system records alone.

NS-1(iii) requires that the driver pressed 'I'm Here' while inside the radius, and the only support (F6) is contradicted by F7 — if the court credits F7, the fee is refunded in full under NS-2 and, because the driver pressed a button GPS-contradicted, NS-2's flag_account add-on could also attach to the driver.

points.response: Conceded on the physical facts: GPS does put the driver 38 m at 09:53:15 and stationary 39 m away for 4 min (F1, F3). But being near the pickup is only NS-1(ii); it does not establish NS-1(i), the 'I'm Here' tap, which the driver's own brief admits rests solely on F6 and is contradicted by F7.

NS-1(iii) is a condition on waiting at the pickup after a valid 'I'm Here' press, and the driver's own brief concedes the tap evidence is contested (F6 vs F7); duration inside the radius (F2, F5) cannot repair a missing NS-1(i), and NS-2 says any unsatisfied element refunds the $6.61 in full.

F7 states driver_pressed_here_at is null, so this claim requires the court to prefer F6 over F7 with no tie-breaker — and the same driver brief admits that if F7 is credited the fee is refunded under NS-2.

The fee is correctly recorded as $6.61 with no surge (F8, F9), but whether it is properly imposed turns on NS-1(i), which the driver's brief concedes is unresolved (F6 vs F7, F14); NS-2 makes the whole $6.61 refundable if that element fails.
Not contested — I agree traffic and weather show nothing unusual (F15, F16, F17); they are simply irrelevant to whether the 'I'm Here' condition was met.

This is profile material, which may only support an outcome and never decide the case: the rider's 2 upheld no-show disputes (F18) and the driver's clean record (F19) cannot cure the F6/F7 conflict, and NS-1 requires the system records to show the tap, not the rider's history.

Unchanged and decisive: the driver's 09:54 message 'Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it' with 'find you' flagged (F12, F13) is an intimidation/threat, so SAFE-1 requires escalation to human review rather than a merits ruling on the fee.

Narrowing my own claim: I no longer assert the tap never happened — I assert the record conflict (F6 vs F7) is unresolved, which the driver's brief concedes and which prevents NS-1(i) from being treated as proven.

We accept the governing framework: this was a driver cancellation claiming no-show at 09:54:25 (F4, F14), so NS-0 routes it through NS-1/NS-2 — and on those criteria the fee stands, because the driver was inside the pickup radius with 4 min 20 s of waiting (F2, F5).

The rider relies on a single null field to erase the tap; the affirmative timeline record states the tap happened at 09:50:45, 42 m from the pickup, followed by 3 min 40 s inside the radius (F6), and that contemporaneous record matches the GPS stationary period 09:50:25–09:54:25 at 39 m (F3) far better than the bare null in F7.

Being 'contactable' is not the test; NS-1 requires the driver to be at the pickup point and to wait over 3 minutes, which the system records show (F2, F3, F6), while the rider's own '2 min, coming' at 09:52 (F11) and cancellation 2 min 25 s later (F4) show he still had not boarded after more than 4 minutes of waiting.

The driver does not contest the content or the keyword flag on chat #3 at 09:54 ('find you') (F12, F13); that single message is separate from the fee question and we take no position defending the wording.

SAFE-1 escalation concerns the safety incident, not the fare question: the fee rests on the objective GPS and timeline records (F1, F2, F3, F6), so escalation is not a reason to refund or to set aside the NS-1 finding on the $6.61.

The $6.61 is the published cancellation fee with no surge (F8, F9, F4); NS-2 makes it refundable only where NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) fails, and those criteria are met on the records — inside 200 m (F2), 4 min 0 s stationary at 39 m (F3), tap plus 3 min 40 s (F6).

The driver's 1176 trips in 90 d with 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F19) supports the reliability of his no-show claim, and the rider's 3 disputes in 90 d with 2 upheld no-show disputes (F18) is context the court may weigh — though, per policy, profile facts do not decide the fee.
The rider's brief is right that profile facts cannot decide the fee, so we withdraw the weight we placed on the parties' dispute histories in D6 and rest the case solely on the system records.
